finding.title: Rename the 'shows three Switch widgets' test in notifications_screen_l1_test.dart to match its findsNWidgets(4) assertion

evidence.quote: testWidgets('shows three Switch widgets (reminder, streak alert, reward)', (

finding.why: The test's own inline comment (line 190) admits the count is 4 ("Three per-preference switches plus one in DeviceNotificationToggle"), a leftover from before the device-level toggle (layer 1 / DEC-27) was added. Anyone reading the test name without the assertion gets the wrong mental model of the screen, and a future edit that trims the count back to 3 would pass the misleadingly-named test while silently dropping the device toggle.
finding.recommendation: Rename to something like "shows four Switch widgets (reminder, streak alert, reward, device toggle)".
acceptance_criteria: Test title reflects the literal 4 in findsNWidgets(4); assertion unchanged.

finding.title: Deduplicate the MockNotificationGateway class shared verbatim by notifications_screen_test.dart and ws5_two_layers_test.dart

evidence.quote: class MockNotificationGateway extends Mock implements NotificationGateway {}
class MockNotificationGateway extends Mock implements NotificationGateway {}

finding.why: Two files under the same feature independently declare an identical top-level `MockNotificationGateway` class. Harmless today, but the digest's dedup pass will flag it as a duplicate top-level symbol, and if the two copies ever drift (e.g. one gets extra default stubs), the same name means different behavior depending on which file's test you're reading.
finding.recommendation: Move the class into a small shared test-support file under test/features/notifications/ (e.g. support/mock_notification_gateway.dart) and import it from both.
acceptance_criteria: Only one MockNotificationGateway declaration exists; both test files import it.
(Rule-0, Pending) AG-4 duplicate-symbol audit no longer lists MockNotificationGateway as duplicated.

finding.title: Register needs_flutter/notifications/notifications_screen_l1 tags in dart_test.yaml to silence unknown-tag warnings
finding.why: learning_tracker/dart_test.yaml's `tags:` block enumerates ~60 epic/story/misc tags but not `needs_flutter`, `notifications`, or `notifications_screen_l1`. Running any of these 3 files (verified for 2 of them) prints "Warning: A tag was used that wasn't specified in dart_test.yaml" on every invocation. It's non-fatal today, but a growing pile of unregistered-tag warnings trains developers/agents to ignore the warning stream, which is exactly where a genuine typo'd or newly-broken tag filter would also hide.
finding.recommendation: Add `needs_flutter:`, `notifications:`, and `notifications_screen_l1:` to dart_test.yaml's tags: block (and any other in-use-but-unregistered tags found elsewhere in the suite).
acceptance_criteria: dart_test.yaml lists needs_flutter, notifications, and notifications_screen_l1.
`flutter test test/features/notifications/` runs with no "A tag was used that wasn't specified in dart_test.yaml" warning.

finding.title: Replace ws5_per_profile_test.dart's tautological payload-format assertions with real NotificationGateway verification
finding.why: None of the 3 tests in the 'notification payload format' group ever construct a NotificationGateway or call scheduleDailyReminderForProfile/scheduleStreakAlertForProfile (confirmed: no NotificationGateway( appears anywhere in this file). Two of the three just re-interpolate the same '$dailyReminderPayload:$profileId' formula the source uses and compare it to a literal, or hand-write a `parts` list and assert facts about the literal they just wrote three lines earlier -- these can never fail regardless of what NotificationGateway actually does, so despite the docstring's claim to verify "per-profile payload format", they add file weight without adding protection. The real protection already exists properly (mocked zonedSchedule + captureAny) in the sibling notification_gateway_test.dart:320-416 outside this batch, which is why this is hygiene/redundancy (P3) rather than a live coverage gap.
finding.recommendation: Either delete these two redundant tests (coverage already exists in notification_gateway_test.dart) or rewrite them to construct a NotificationGateway with a mocked FlutterLocalNotificationsPlugin and assert on the captured `payload:` argument from scheduleDailyReminderForProfile, matching this file's own '(good)' ID-allocation tests which do call the real functions.
acceptance_criteria: Remaining payload-format tests in this file (if kept) invoke NotificationGateway rather than re-deriving the expected string independently.
Red-first check: temporarily change the separator/format in notification_gateway.dart's per-profile payload construction and confirm whichever tests remain go red.

finding.title: Stop relying on find.byKey(...).last for time-row lookups in notifications_screen_l1_test.dart and notifications_screen_test.dart
finding.why: _SettingsTimeRow (learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/presentation/screens/notifications_screen.dart:306, `return ListTile(key: key, ...)`) forwards its own key onto the inner ListTile it builds, so Key('reminder_time')/Key('streak_alert_time') each match 2 elements in the tree. All 8 sites paper over that with `.last`, trusting find.byKey's traversal order to put the ListTile after its wrapper -- an implementation detail, not a documented Flutter API contract -- while the very same file already uses a robust, order-independent alternative for the Switch rows (e.g. l1_test.dart:218-220, `find.descendant(of: reminderRow, matching: find.byType(Switch))`). If the match order ever flipped, `.last` would silently resolve to the wrapper widget and the ensuing `tester.widget<ListTile>(...)` cast would throw, breaking otherwise-unrelated tests with a confusing error.
finding.recommendation: Match the ListTile the same way the Switch rows already do -- e.g. `find.widgetWithText(ListTile, l10n.notifReminderTime)` or, on the production side, stop forwarding `key` to the inner ListTile in _SettingsTimeRow and instead expose a distinct key for it -- so the finder resolves to exactly one widget without depending on registration order.
acceptance_criteria: Time-row assertions no longer call `.last` on a byKey finder with 2 matches.
The 8 call sites are updated or, if `.last` is kept, each carries a comment justifying why the order is guaranteed.
